paths.description: Public landing page and primary join/discovery entry. Tested desktop, 360px mobile, dark, high contrast, reduced motion, non-JS, performance, network, privacy, image and memory conditions.
Representative public category/listing archetype and inspiration-browsing journey.
Representative authentication form and account-entry flow, including empty submission and keyboard focus.

findings.summary: The public experience does not adapt to dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; DOM computed style reports a white html background and color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Route and major state changes do not expose View Transition styling.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found reduced-motion, container-query, scroll-state, scroll-marker and anchor-positioning rules, but no view-transition rules on the sampled public shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for major route/state changes, gated by reduced-motion.

findings.summary: A consent modal obscures the primary page content on initial load.
findings.evidence: Desktop captures of the home and shopping pages show a centered modal plus full-page scrim before any interaction. Reject is available and visually comparable, but the content remains blocked.
findings.suggestedFix: Where lawful, keep essential consent choices concise and avoid blocking non-tracking content; preserve equally prominent reject/customise actions.

findings.summary: Modal surfaces use custom role=dialog containers instead of the native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence reports no <dialog> while a fixed [role=dialog] fills the viewport; the sampled page also had no popover or details primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal flows and popover/details for transient or disclosure UI, retaining labelled focus management.

findings.summary: The homepage overflows and clips core content at a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout evidence measured scrollWidth 929px against a 360px visual viewport, 569px horizontal overflow; the mobile screenshot clips the hero heading and secondary CTA.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed desktop sizing, constrain flex/grid children with intrinsic sizing, and verify the entire core flow at 320–360px.

findings.summary: Public discovery journeys are interrupted by an immediate account wall.
findings.evidence: The Ideas page displays useful categories behind a full modal login wall on first load, preventing the representative inspiration-browsing flow without account action.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow a meaningful public browse path before authentication, then request sign-in in context for save/personalisation actions.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance and visual stability are far outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 14,865ms, CLS 0.797 and TBT 509.5ms (performance score 0.19). A separate trace measured LCP 3,098ms and TBT 111.79ms, confirming run variability but still showing blocking work.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, reserve media space, prioritise the LCP asset, and reduce startup work; validate against field data and repeat lab runs.

findings.summary: Large unused JavaScript and long main-thread tasks burden startup.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 946,268 bytes of unused JavaScript and 27,543 bytes of unused CSS; trace recorded two long tasks up to 117.82ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route code, conditionally load authentication/analytics dependencies, and break or schedule long tasks by priority.

findings.summary: Most sampled images lack alternative text.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 32 of 35 images without alt text on the landing experience. These visuals communicate inspiration categories and are not all safely decorative.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide concise contextual alt text for meaningful pins/category images and alt="" only for truly decorative duplicates.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime and network errors during a normal load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a Google FedCM NetworkError, two first-party 404 responses and an identity-provider sign-in error.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle expected identity-provider states without console.error and repair or suppress failed first-party resource requests.

findings.summary: The canonical homepage is effectively a JavaScript shell for non-JS crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability evidence found only 1% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML, no raw h1, and isJsShell=true; the crawler screenshot says Pinterest requires JavaScript. Ideas and Shopping fare better at 48% and 62%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the homepage purpose, headings, primary links and representative content; hydrate enhancements rather than replacing core content.

findings.summary: Cookie and browser-policy settings leave avoidable security gaps.
findings.evidence: Cookies evidence flags _b and _routing_id without Secure and all four cookies as SameSite=None; headers include CSP/HSTS/nosniff/frame protection but omit Permissions-Policy and retain unsafe-inline allowances.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark every HTTPS cookie Secure, narrow SameSite where possible, add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and continue reducing CSP unsafe-inline dependencies.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated landing load has a broad third-party and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Trackers evidence observed 10 third-party origins and known Pinterest tracking hosts; most requests were to pinimg plus Google/recaptcha dependencies before account use.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and defer non-essential third parties until consent/context, batch analytics, and document the minimum data purpose for each origin.

findings.summary: Landing-page images are oversized, legacy-formatted and insufficiently deferred.
findings.evidence: Images evidence found 27/35 oversized, 35/35 legacy JPG, 34 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 11 missing srcset, and all 35 without explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources, add intrinsic dimensions, choose correct srcset sizes, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Repeated feed-style scrolling retains substantial additional heap.
findings.evidence: After ten bottom/top scroll cycles, heap self size grew from 60.1MB to 66.8MB (+11.3%), node count from 897,011 to 1,058,064 (+18.0%), objects from 93,574 to 170,245, and closures from 48,729 to 62,773. This may include intentional lazy-loaded content, so confidence is medium.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat the scenario in one instrumented session with GC and stabilization between cycles; bound caches and clean up observers/listeners for offscreen feed content.

findings.summary: Empty login submission provides no observable error or required-field state.
findings.evidence: The login probe found email/password required=false, aria-invalid=false, and no role=alert or aria-live error after activating submit with empty values. Focus styling itself was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints, validate after interaction, set aria-invalid, and announce specific errors through a live region while moving focus predictably.

findings.summary: The sampled sign-in flow offers passwords and federated/QR options but no visible passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login screenshot and DOM show email/password, Google and QR-code choices; no passkey/WebAuthn option was present on the representative authentication surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in and registration alongside recovery-compatible existing methods, with conditional UI where supported.

findings.summary: The initial heap/DOM footprint is heavy for a public landing page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 897,011 nodes, 3,902,046 edges and 60.1MB self size before an authenticated feed is opened.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit startup object ownership and delay feed, auth and analytics graphs until needed; set a bounded heap/DOM budget for the unauthenticated shell.

Recover Core Web Vitals and reduce startup JavaScript
Make core homepage and discovery content server-rendered and publicly reachable
Optimise and correctly describe responsive imagery
Harden cookies, browser policies and third-party loading
Add humane login errors and passkey authentication
Investigate and bound landing/feed memory growth
Respect dark mode and modernise transitions/dialog primitives
Clean normal-load console and resource errors
